# frostmoln_messaging_vhost (Resource)

Manages a virtual host (vhost) on a managed messaging (LavinMQ) instance. A vhost is an isolated namespace of exchanges, queues and bindings; grant a `frostmoln_messaging_user` access to it with a `frostmoln_messaging_permission`.

Create and destroy wait until the platform has applied the change on the broker. Operations on one instance run one at a time, so the provider serialises every vhost, user and permission change per instance (other instances still proceed in parallel). Destroying a vhost DELETES EVERY MESSAGE IN IT, and is refused while any permission still names it.

Import with `<instance_id>/<name>`.

**Authoritative scope** — who owns what on this resource, declared in `internal/scopedecl` and machine-checked against the schema.

**Create-immutable** — `instance_id`, `name`: a vhost is identified by its name on its instance, and the broker has no rename; changing either creates a new, empty vhost and deletes every message in this one.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A vhost on a managed messaging instance. Destroying it deletes every message
# in it, and is refused while a permission still names it.
resource "frostmoln_messaging_vhost" "orders" {
  instance_id = frostmoln_messaging_instance.broker.id
  name        = "orders"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (String) The id of the `frostmoln_messaging_instance` the vhost lives on. Changing it creates the vhost on the other instance and deletes this one.
- `name` (String) The vhost's name: 1 to 64 characters of `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_` and `-`, starting with a letter or digit, unique on the instance regardless of case (`Orders` cannot be created while `orders` exists); a change in case is a different name. Changing it replaces the vhost and deletes every message in the old one.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the vhost was created.
- `failure_message` (String) The last failed change's reason in words, or null.
- `failure_reason` (String) The stable code of the vhost's last failed change (for example `IN_FLIGHT` or `BROKER_REFUSED`), or null. Every code but `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` means the broker was left unchanged.
- `id` (String) The vhost's Terraform id, `<instance_id>/<name>`.
- `status` (String) The vhost's status: `pending` while the platform applies a create, `ready`, `deleting`, or `error` when a create failed (the vhost is absent or its state unknown; the next apply deletes and re-creates it).
- `updated_at` (String) When the vhost last changed.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) How long the provider waits for the create operation to converge before giving up (e.g. "45m", "2h").
- `delete` (String) How long the provider waits for the delete to complete before giving up (e.g. "30m").
- `update` (String) How long the provider waits for an update (resize, in-place change) to converge before giving up (e.g. "30m").

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with the composite ID {instance_id}/{name}.
terraform import frostmoln_messaging_vhost.orders 51455a51-db3d-4231-ac27-4fee2553c15f/orders
```
